newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti chief wants IT sector regrouping.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti chief wants IT sector regrouping.

text.p: Italy needs an industrial policy which would allow the creation of a large information technology group capable of competing on a global scale, Olivetti chairman Roberto Colaninno was quoted as saying in a newspaper.
Colaninno told Il Sole financial daily he saw Finsiel, the IT systems subsidiary of state telecoms holding Stet, as part of such a company as well as other firms.

"If one wants to be a global operator on the information service market, if one wants to be competitive in quality and costs, one needs to have a global perimeter of business, equal to those of the principal U.S. sector leaders," he said.
"When I talk about a new industrial policy, I am referring to the globalisation of various realities operating in Italy and technologically ready for the challenge," he said.

"The government needs to show itself capable of a real industrial plan, promoting the birth of a big information group with the dimensions and technology allowing it to measure up to anyone," he said, adding it was "a group in which I see Finsiel without doubt but also other players."

Carlo De Benedetti, now honorary chairman of Olivetti after years at its helm, was reported at the weekend to have decided his industrial holding CIR would keep a five percent stake in Olivetti, after being asked by the government to do so.

Colaninno said he was pleased an important shareholder like CIR had decided not to get rid of its stake and said he viewed the possible reasons behind the government's request and De Benedetti's decision as highly important.

He noted Olivetti was transforming itself into a company of new dimensions and said it was the only private Italian company already really active in the field of telecommunications and the only Italian multinational in information technology.
"It represents - it has already represented with Omnitel and Infostrada - an interesting opportunity for investment for big foreign groups like Bell Atlantic and Mannesmann," he said.
This along with Olivetti's crisis last year had, in his opinion, brought the government to recognise that Italy needed to redefine its industrial policy for the information sector.

"It's a sector in which there are lots of protagonists but they are all too small. Joining them together, developing possible synergies, using existing technology could give precious opportunities of growth in a strong U.S. market and in expansion also in Europe," he said.
